x-m-el-cul-01.title: Credit Card Really Be “Golden Ratio”?
x-m-el-cul-01.topic: Ratio, Symmetry, and Patterns in Art and Everyday Life
x-m-el-cul-01.goal: Calculate ratios and compare dem with a claim, then set your own rule for how much difference you go accept before saying “na golden ratio.”
x-m-el-cul-01.material: Blog post talk: “Credit card na rectangle 85.6mm by 53.98mm, and long side to short side ratio na golden ratio.” Golden ratio na (1 plus square root of 5) divided by 2, about 1.618. Compare these size ratios (long : short): A4 paper 297mm : 210mm, postcard 148mm : 100mm, and monitor with ratio 16 to 10, 16 : 10.
x-m-el-cul-01.thinking.1: Set and Use a Tolerance Rule
x-m-el-cul-01.prereq.0: Find Ratio of Two Lengths by Division (middle school level)
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s1.prompt: You wan evaluate blog claim “Credit card na golden ratio rectangle.” Divide long side by short side and choose best evaluation.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s1.hint.0: Divide long side by short side and put result beside 1.618.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s1.hint.1: Think separately whether two values “equal” and how much dem different.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s1.o.a: Quotient 1.586 round to 1.6, so you fit say exactly golden ratio
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s1.r.a: You use rounded value wey look same as proof of “equal.” Check whether conclusion change according to how many digits you round.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s1.o.b: 1.586 and 1.618 different, so credit card no get anything to do with golden ratio
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s1.r.b: You split am into only “equal / totally different.” You no think about how big di difference be.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s1.o.c: Ratio na about 1.586, different from 1.618, so “close” na more accurate word
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s1.r.c: You compare calculated value with claim value and tell “equal” apart from “close.”
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s1.o.d: Ratio measured in mm change when convert to cm, so values no fit compare
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s1.r.d: You think ratio change when unit change. Check wetin happen to ratio of two lengths measured in same unit when convert unit.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s1.explain: 85.6÷53.98 na about 1.586, about 2% different from golden ratio 1.618. Here, “close to golden ratio” honest pass “exactly golden ratio.”
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s2.prompt: You set rule: “If long side ÷ short side differ from 1.618 by within 3%, e close to golden ratio.” Choose all cases wey fit be called close. (3% of 1.618 na about 0.049.)
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s2.hint.0: Change each case ratio to decimal.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s2.hint.1: Subtract 0.049 from 1.618 and add 0.049 to find allowed range yourself, then check whether each ratio dey inside.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s2.r.a: Check again how you read difference when finding ratio and comparing with standard. Work out whether difference between this value and 1.618 dey inside allowed range.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s2.r.b: You find ratio and compare difference from 1.618 with allowed range.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s2.r.c: Check whether you work out if difference between postcard ratio and 1.618 dey inside allowed range. Feeling say dem look alike no same as comparing with rule.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s2.r.d: You change 16÷10 to decimal and compare with standard.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s2.explain: Only credit card, 1.586 (about 2.0% difference), and monitor, 1.6 (about 1.1%), dey within 3%. A4 na about 1.414 (about 12.6%) and postcard na 1.48 (about 8.5%), outside range.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s3.prompt: Tolerance (here 3%) na standard I choose. Write one or two sentences why you must set tolerance before saying “na golden ratio,” and wetin to watch out for when setting rule.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s3.hint.0: First write one sentence why judgment without standard be problem.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s3.hint.1: Imagine wetin happen to A4 and postcard if you set very wide standard (for example 20%).
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You give as reason say “exactly same value” hardly ever happen in real life?
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You write wetin happen if standard too wide or too narrow?
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You fit explain how credit card and postcard separate under your rule?
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s3.model.0: Measured values always get error and rulers no exact, so exact equal values hardly ever happen. Set tolerance like 1% or 3% first, then say close if e dey inside. If standard too wide, nearly every rectangle become golden ratio.
x-m-el-cul-01.s.s3.model.1: Rectangle wey exactly 1.618 hardly ever exist for real, so you need set range like within 5%. But if range na 10%, postcard (about 8.5% difference) enter too and rule too loose.

x-m-el-cul-02.material: Dem often use symmetry for traditional patterns and building design. One student make table summarizing shape symmetry. Line-symmetric shape get line of symmetry wey make both halves overlap when folded; point-symmetric shape overlap itself after half turn (180°) around a point. One table line get mistake.

x-m-el-cul-03.topic: Ratio, Symmetry, and Patterns in Art and Everyday Life
x-m-el-cul-03.title: Design Pattern for Sidewalk with 100 Blocks
x-m-el-cul-03.goal: Design different repeating patterns wey meet ratio and length rules together, and explain common rule for possible periods.
x-m-el-cul-03.material: For row of 100 sidewalk blocks, red and blue blocks alternate. Pattern use “r red blocks followed by (p−r) blue blocks” as one group, then repeat. Conditions: (1) p na whole number from 2 to 50; r na whole number from 1 to less than p. (2) Last group no cut off; all 100 blocks end exactly. (3) Exactly 40 red blocks (40% of total).
x-m-el-cul-03.thinking.1: Find Wetin Solutions Get in Common
x-m-el-cul-03.prereq.0: Ratio (part of whole) and Whole-number Multiplication and Division
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s0.prompt: Make we arrange am first. For exactly 40 out of 100 cells to be red, wetin condition must one bundle (p cells) meet? (All 100 cells end exactly at bundle end.)
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s0.hint.0: First write number of groups (100÷p), then multiply by red blocks per group.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s0.hint.1: Write equation where total red cells na 40, then turn am to relationship between r and p.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s0.o.a: Fraction of red cells in one bundle, r÷p, must be 40%
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s0.r.a: Because bundle repeat same pattern, you see rate in one bundle equal rate for whole row.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s0.o.b: Ratio of red to blue in one bundle, r:(p−r), must be 40:100
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s0.r.b: You mix ratio comparing red with blue with share of red out of whole. 40% mean share of red cells among all 100.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s0.o.c: Number of bundles, 100÷p, must equal red cell number in one bundle, r
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s0.r.c: You mix bundle number and red cell number. Think how many red cells dey inside one bundle.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s0.o.d: Red cell number in one bundle, r, must be 40
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s0.r.d: You treat red cells in one bundle same as total red cells. Think how many times bundle repeat.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s0.explain: Since group repeat same way, if red blocks na 40% of whole, dem must be 40% in one group too. This na condition between r and p.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.prompt: Make three different patterns wey meet every condition. p na blocks in one group, r na red blocks in one group.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.hint.0: First write possible p values wey let 100 blocks end exactly with groups of p blocks.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.hint.1: For each possible p, find group number and find r needed to get 40 red blocks.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.var.r: Red blocks in one group, r
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.ok.c1: p and r na whole numbers.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.fail.c1: p and r must be whole numbers.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.fail.c2: p na 2 to 50, and r must be at least 1 but smaller than p.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.fail.c3: Some groups get cut. 100 blocks must divide evenly into groups of p blocks.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.fail.c4: Red blocks no be 40. Check by multiplying group count by r.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.explain: (p, r) = (5, 2), (10, 4), (20, 8), (25, 10), (50, 20) all meet di conditions. For example, if p=20 and r=8, groups na 5 and red blocks 8×5=40.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.because.prompt: Di p values you find all multiples of which number? Explain in one or two sentences why.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.because.hint.0: Change r × (number of groups)=40 into equation for r.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.because.hint.1: Choose some factors of 100, like p=4 or p=20, calculate r, then separate cases where r natural number or not.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.because.selfAssess.0: Your reason connect to ratio say "red blocks na 2/5 of total"?
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.because.selfAssess.1: You explain using case like "p=3, r=1.2" where r no be natural number?
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.because.model.0: Red blocks na 40% of whole, wey be 2/5, so red blocks must be 2/5 inside one group too. For r to be natural number, p must multiple of 5.
x-m-el-cul-03.s.s1.because.model.1: If r×(100÷p)=40, then r=0.4×p. For 0.4×p to be natural, p must multiple of 5.

x-m-el-cul-09.title: Make one-measure rhythm yourself
x-m-el-cul-09.goal: Make several rhythms yourself wey meet total-beats condition, and explain why some notes get limit on how many you fit use.
x-m-el-cul-09.material: One measure of 4/4 time get 4 beats. Quarter note take 1 beat, eighth note take 0.5 beat, and half note take 2 beats. You wan make rhythm wey fill one measure with exactly 4 beats using notes only, no rests. So e no monotonous, use at least 1 quarter note, at least 2 eighth notes, and at least 4 notes altogether.
x-m-el-cul-09.thinking.1: Think of method to find dem without missing any.
x-m-el-cul-09.thinking.2: Connect fraction and decimal sums with whole-number conditions.
x-m-el-cul-09.prereq.1: The note lengths dey explained for the material.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s0.prompt: You wan find all rhythms wey fit one measure with 4 beats, without missing any. Which method best?
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s0.hint.0: Start by finding the greatest number of half notes wey fit enter.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s0.hint.1: Fix one case, then investigate every possible combination for that case all the way.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s0.o.a: Choose notes as dem come mind, add the beats, and collect the ones wey make 4.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s0.r.a: You fit find some, but you no know whether you find all.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s0.o.b: Fix number of half notes, then for each case check every possible quarter and eighth-note combination.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s0.r.b: This method fix the count of one kind in order and investigate each case all the way so you no miss any.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s0.o.c: Fix number of half notes, and for each case find only one quarter/eighth combination, then move to next case.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s0.r.c: Splitting into cases good, but finding only one inside each case make you miss other solutions in the same case.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s0.o.d: Fix number of quarter notes and stop when one case come up.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s0.r.d: If you find one and stop, you no know whether more answers dey.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s0.explain: If you fix one note type count as 0, then 1, then 2, and investigate the others in each case, you fit check whether you find all.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.prompt: Make three different rhythms wey meet the conditions. a na number of quarter notes, b eighth notes, c half notes.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.hint.0: Fix half-note number c as 0 or 1, then find ways to fill remaining beats with quarter and eighth notes.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.hint.1: After you find one, change am and keep same beat count, like reduce eighth notes by 2 and increase quarter notes by 1.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.ok.c1: The counts na integers 0 or more.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.fail.c1: Note counts must be integers 0 or more.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.ok.c2: At least 1 quarter note and at least 2 eighth notes.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.fail.c2: Must use at least 1 quarter note and at least 2 eighth notes.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.fail.c3: The beat total no be 4. Multiply each note count by its beat value and add.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.fail.c4: You must use at least 4 notes altogether.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.explain: (a, b, c) = (3, 2, 0), (2, 4, 0), (1, 6, 0), (1, 2, 1) na all four wey meet every condition. For example, (1, 2, 1) na 1 + 2×0.5 + 2 = 4 beats.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.because.prompt: Use one or two sentences explain why rhythm no fit get odd number of eighth notes.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.because.hint.0: Find how many beats notes take if 1 eighth note or 3 dey.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.because.hint.1: First check whether the other notes take whole number of beats.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.because.selfAssess.0: You use the fact say other notes' beats na whole numbers?
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.because.selfAssess.1: You talk how many eighth notes must join to make one whole beat?
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.because.model.0: Quarter and half notes take whole number of beats, so remaining eighth notes must make whole number too. Two eighth notes make 1 beat, so eighth-note count must be even.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.because.model.1: One eighth note na 0.5 beat, so odd number go leave .5 in total and no fit make 4 beats. So count must be even.
x-m-el-cul-09.s.s1.because.model.2: Two eighth notes together make one beat, so odd number leave half a beat, and you no fit fill 4 whole beats.

x-m-el-cul-04.goal: To judge cause claim based on "garbage went down after campaign," sort needed info, and write specifically how conclusion change depending on result.
x-m-el-cul-04.material: District office run recycling campaign in 2024. Their data say monthly average household waste drop from 1,200 tons in 2023 (year before campaign) to 1,080 tons in 2025, decrease 10% (10% of 1,200 na 120). Office website say, "Recycling campaign reduce waste by 10%."
